items.title: Joe Segal — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Don Moye was a marvelous percussionist.

ctx.x: Yeah, yeah. I booked him mostly because of John Gilmore and Pat Patrick on the band.
Ok. I see you also booked the Art Ensemble of Chicago.

Yeah, I dug them. They had some humor about them and some... Lester Bowie has a humor about him. He wasn’t all “oh boy, this is,” you know. And they could play. Don Moye was a marvelous percussionist. And I had heard avant-garde before that; the ACM wasn’t the first ones. Joe Daly and Hal Russell had stuff going way before that. And it was ok, but they came from the straight-ahead stuff, and that’s the kind of avant-garde I like. It was played by people who know how to play straight ahead, because I feel to have…
